messages:
jordan: trying to set up redwoodctl on my new macbook (arm, Ventura). `brew install redwoodctl` finishes but `redwoodctl` command is missing from PATH. also `redwoodctl login` opens browser but it never completes the redirect, stuck on 'waiting for auth'. anyone seen this?
jordan: also when i try `redwoodctl dev start` it fails with EADDRINUSE even though nothing obvious is on 8910 or 3000. super confusing.
marta: @jordan can you paste `which redwoodctl` and `brew --prefix`? my hunch is Homebrew path confusion between /usr/local and /opt/homebrew on arm.
jordan: `which redwoodctl` -> nothing
jordan: `brew --prefix` -> /opt/homebrew
jordan: installed with `brew install redwoodctl/redwood/redwoodctl` (followed the formula). install logs show this at the end: `Warning: redwoodctl was installed into /opt/homebrew/Cellar/redwoodctl/0.9.4; bin not linked`
marta: ok that explains the PATH. try `brew link --overwrite redwoodctl` or add `/opt/homebrew/bin` to your PATH. on some setups the formula doesn't auto-link.
samir: re: dev start, can you paste the `redwoodctl dev start` error? EADDRINUSE usually means local docker compose or some other process is binding. I had docker desktop forwarding that grabbed :3000 even when no containers were running. try `lsof -i :3000` and `lsof -i :8910`.
jordan: `redwoodctl dev start` output: "error: could not bind to 127.0.0.1:8910: address already in use"
mike: quick workaround for the auth redirect: run `redwoodctl login --no-browser` which prints a device code and a URL you can open on another machine. that helped when our mac's default browser profile was blocking the callback. not sure if that's available in your install though.
jordan: `redwoodctl --version` still gives "command not found" after linking. had to restart shell to pick up PATH. after restart, `redwoodctl login` now starts oauth flow and opens browser, but browser shows "waiting for device confirmation" and the CLI still waits.
marta: sometimes corporate browser extensions block the callback. try the `--no-browser` flow mike mentioned or `redwoodctl login --profile dev --no-browser` to make sure the creds are written to the dev profile.
jordan: ran `redwoodctl login --no-browser`, got a code, pasted in browser on my phone, confirmed — CLI printed "login complete". creds land in `~/.redwood/config` under a `profiles` block but i noticed the file is owned by root? file perms show `-rw-r--r--  root root`. i installed via sudo earlier (no idea why).
marta: ah the classic sudo vs brew mismatch. fix with `sudo chown $(whoami) ~/.redwood -R` and avoid sudo for future installs. i'll add a note to the install docs.
samir: also for the port conflict: `redwoodctl dev start --port 4000` works as a quick test. long-term we should make the port configurable in `dev-config.yaml` and add a clearer error hint. filing a small issue.
mike: fwiw, for CI/local pairing i keep `REDWOOD_DEV_PORT=4000` in `.env.local` so docker-compose and redwoodctl don't collide. works well.
devex-bot: internal doc: https://redwood.company/docs/devex/redwoodctl-install-troubleshoot — covers Homebrew path, linking, and headless login. also linked an issue: https://redwood.company/issue/INF-4726 (devctl: make dev port configurable)
jordan: thanks all — fixed PATH/linking, used `--no-browser` to complete auth, chowned ~/.redwood, and started dev on 4000. summary for the thread: 1) check brew link or PATH, 2) use `--no-browser` if callback gets blocked, 3) chown ~/.redwood if you used sudo, 4) override dev port to avoid docker conflicts. posting here in case others hit same combo. :thumbsup:
marta: great writeup — i'll add a short section to the quickstart and link to the internal doc. can you drop the exact `lsof` output here before you close so i can copy it?
jordan: `COMMAND   PID   USER   FD   TYPE DEVICE SIZE/OFF NODE NAME
node    4523 jordan   23u  IPv4 0x...      0t0 TCP 127.0.0.1:3000 (LISTEN)`
marta: perfect, thanks. will follow up in the quickstart PR. :sparkles:
